claims: Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged investment accounts for U.S. citizen children under 18.
Trump Accounts were established by the 2025 "One Big Beautiful Bill Act."
Trump Accounts provide a $1,000 government-seeded investment vehicle.
Trump Accounts are for children born between 2025–2028.
Parents, family, or employers can contribute up to $5,000 annually per child to Trump Accounts.
Trump Accounts receive a one-time $1,000 deposit from the Treasury.
The one-time $1,000 Treasury deposit for Trump Accounts is for children born January 1, 2025 – December 31, 2028.
Funds in Trump Accounts generally cannot be withdrawn before age 18.
Non-qualified expenses from Trump Accounts incur some tax penalties.
Parents can make an election on IRS Form 4547 for Trump Accounts starting with the 2026 tax year.
Eligibility for Trump Accounts is for U.S. citizen children under 18 with a Social Security Number.
Parents or legal guardians act as custodians of Trump Accounts until the child turns 18.
At age 18, Trump Accounts transition to follow traditional IRA rules.
The Michael and Susan Dell Foundation has pledged additional funding for specific, eligible children.
